task: Stage 1 workforce identity authority foundation with safe return targets, canonical privileged sign-in recovery, credential completion, and first-owner activation.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This isolated authority unit changes privileged sign-in continuation, password recovery and credential establishment. Incorrect behavior could create an open redirect, mix shopper session state into workforce credential mutation, or create a second authentication authority.

acceptanceCriteria: A shared workforce return-target authority accepts only /admin, /admin/* and exact /storefront-template-preview continuations.
The dedicated workforce login uses the shared sanitizer and can safely carry an approved continuation into the existing WorkforceAuthForm.
Workforce password recovery returns only to an auth-owned credential completion route.
Credential completion accepts invite or recovery modes, requires callback evidence beyond a pre-existing session, updates the Supabase password, then re-enters canonical workforce login.
First-owner activation is available as an auth-owned component that checks the existing server-side owner claim before Supabase signup and never signs an existing user in directly.
Existing server RBAC, tenant authority, shopper AuthForm and parked AAL2 enforcement remain unchanged.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the only session, password and MFA authority.
Server-owned platform_operators and role_bindings authorities remain unchanged.
A pre-existing shopper session alone cannot authorize workforce credential mutation.
No middleware authorization authority is added.
The parked PR #858 is not modified or activated.

failureModes: A crafted continuation escapes the local workforce route allowlist.
Recovery falls back into shopper credential UX.
A pre-existing shopper session makes the workforce credential route ready without invite or recovery callback evidence.
First-owner activation becomes an alternate existing-user sign-in surface.
Credential completion bypasses canonical workforce role/MFA processing after password update.
The isolated authority unit accidentally activates parked AAL2 server enforcement.
edgeCases: Nested admin paths with query strings remain valid.
Exact template-preview path with query parameters remains valid.
Preview-login, fiokom, protocol-relative and absolute external targets are rejected.
PKCE code/token-hash and hash-token callback forms can supply credential link evidence.
A valid new-owner activation session re-enters canonical workforce login rather than entering admin directly.

alternatives.summary: Reuse shopper AuthForm for privileged recovery and invitation completion.
alternatives.reason: This mixes customer and workforce credential semantics.

alternatives.summary: Keep a second platform signInWithPassword implementation.
alternatives.reason: This preserves split privileged authentication authority.

alternatives.summary: Centralize safe continuation, recovery, credential completion and owner activation under the existing auth authority.
alternatives.reason: This isolates the high-risk authority change and preserves downstream wiring for a separate bounded unit.

specialistReviews.finding: All substantive files belong to DOMAIN-IDENTITY.
specialistReviews.resolution: Only auth canonical paths change; downstream presentation and admin wiring remain read-only.

specialistReviews.finding: A pre-existing shopper session must not be sufficient to mutate workforce credentials.
specialistReviews.resolution: Credential completion requires invite/recovery callback evidence before session readiness is accepted.

specialistReviews.finding: High-risk auth authority must be isolated by the production release-risk budget.
specialistReviews.resolution: This unit contains only auth-access-authority substantive files; tests and plan are evidence-neutral.

challenge.scenario: An attacker supplies //evil.example or https://evil.example as next.
challenge.finding: Loose local checks could allow an external continuation.
challenge.resolution: Shared normalization uses the canonical local normalizer plus an exact workforce path allowlist.

challenge.finding: These targets can create loops or mix shopper/workforce UX.
challenge.resolution: Only /admin families and exact /storefront-template-preview are accepted.

challenge.scenario: A workforce user requests password recovery.
challenge.finding: Recovery through shopper AuthForm would recreate split credential authority.
challenge.resolution: WorkforceAuthForm sends recovery to /api/auth/workforce-credential and then canonical workforce login.

challenge.scenario: A shopper session already exists when the workforce credential URL is opened manually.
challenge.finding: Session presence alone could otherwise make password mutation available.
challenge.resolution: Credential form requires callback evidence before consulting the current session.

challenge.scenario: A first-owner activation component is mistaken for a normal platform login.
challenge.finding: It could become a second existing-user password authority.
challenge.resolution: The component exposes signup activation only, checks the owner claim and contains no signInWithPassword path.

challenge.scenario: A successful password update navigates directly into admin.
challenge.finding: That would bypass canonical workforce context and MFA UX.
challenge.resolution: Credential completion navigates to workforceLoginHref(target), not directly to the privileged target.

challenge.scenario: The authority foundation is conflated with PR #858 enforcement.
challenge.finding: Server authorization semantics could be activated prematurely.
challenge.resolution: requireAdmin, middleware and workforce assurance enforcement are read-only and deterministic proof asserts no enforcement activation.

proofPlan: Run the Development Guard against the exact auth-only diff.
Run deterministic workforce auth foundation and existing workforce UX/bridge tests.
Require Production Release Risk Budget to report only auth-access-authority at 5/5 points.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure before integration.

requirements.requirement: Canonical workforce authentication authority safely owns privileged continuation, recovery, credential completion and first-owner activation primitives without changing shopper, RBAC, tenant or parked AAL2 enforcement authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Workforce continuation targets must remain local and limited to approved workforce destinations.
A pre-existing shopper session must not by itself authorize workforce credential mutation.
First-owner activation must not create a second existing-user password-login authority.
Parked server-side AAL2 authorization enforcement must remain inactive.

notes: This transaction is the high-risk auth-authority half of the previously planned workforce entrypoint convergence. It is isolated because Production Release Risk Budget correctly rejected the combined auth/admin/customer/storefront unit. Downstream presentation/admin wiring is intentionally deferred to a second bounded transaction after this authority unit is integrated. Plan Before Code exact-head f19c498 corrected projection scope: auth App Router pages also project storefront-ui impact, canonical negative knowledge expands by SQ-NK-001/SQ-NK-008, high-risk assurance requires pairwise-interactions, and completion source identity is unified with the PO request.
